while a slightly weaker version, where the $J''$-term is weighted with the factor $1/2$, \cite[Theorem A.5]{zbMATH07846602}, is necessary.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract states that the paper proves second-order optimality conditions that are both necessary and sufficient. What the paper establishes is only sufficiency: Assumption 3.6 postulates the joint growth of J' and J'' (eq. (3.5)) and Theorem 3.9 derives local optimality from it; no second-order necessary condition is derived anywhere. Necessity is only cited from other papers, and even there only for a modified condition in which the J''-term is weighted by 1/2. The paper's own introduction states 'sufficient second-order optimality conditions', contradicting the abstract.

failure_location.quote: We derive the existence of optimal solutions and prove first- and -- necessary and sufficient -- second-order optimality conditions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract to claim only 'sufficient second-order optimality conditions' (matching the introduction); no mathematical content changes.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract promises a necessary second-order characterization that the paper never establishes, overstating the optimality-theory content of the manuscript.
issues.title: Abstract claims necessary-and-sufficient second-order optimality conditions
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of the abstract aligns it with what is actually proved; no formal result, guarantee, or rate is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the pair $(\mathbf{y},p) = \mathcal{S}(\mathbf{u})$ uniquely solves \eqref{eq:weak_navier_stokes_eq} with $\mathbf{f}=\mathbf{u}$ in $\mathcal{O}(\bar{\mathbf{y}}) \times \mathcal{O}(\bar{p})$,
We immediately note that problem \eqref{eq:state_equations} may have several solutions.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3.5 (implicit function theorem) yields, for each u in the control neighborhood, a unique solution to the state equation only inside the state neighborhoods O(ȳ) × O(p̄). Weak solutions of the stationary Navier–Stokes equations can be multiple, as the paper itself states when introducing S(u). Therefore the conclusion that S(u) 'is formed solely by the pair (y_u, p_u)' — and in particular that S(ū) is a singleton — is an over-inference: uniqueness is guaranteed only within O(ȳ) × O(p̄), not for the full solution set.

failure_location.quote: We note that Theorem \ref{thm:properties_C_to_S} implies that, for every $\mathbf{u}\in \mathcal{O}(\bar{\mathbf{u}})$, the set $S(\mathbf{u})$ is formed solely by the pair $(\mathbf{y}_{\mathbf{u}},p_{\mathbf{u}})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sentence by the localized statement the implicit function theorem actually gives: for each u in O(ū), (y_u, p_u) = S(u) is the unique solution in O(ȳ) × O(p̄); delete 'In particular, S(ū) = {(ȳ, p̄)}'.
issues.overall_effect: An unsupported global-uniqueness claim about the solution set is asserted; the subsequent analysis of Sections 3–5 does not actually require it, since all arguments are local in the state and control neighborhoods.
issues.title: Global uniqueness of the solution set asserted from a purely local implicit-function theorem
issues.why_classification: Removing or localizing one sentence preserves every labelled result, proof, and guarantee; no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, the error estimate $\|\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{y}_h\|_{\mathbf{L}^{2}(\Omega)} \nlesssim h^{2}\|\mathbf{y}\|_{\mathbf{H}^{2}(\Omega)}$ holds for all $h \in (0, h_{\star})$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs \|\nabla(y_{ū_h} − ȳ_h)\|_{L^{6/5}} ≲ h² to conclude \|∇(ẑ_h − z̄_h)\|_{L²} ≲ h², which is load-bearing for the advertised rate (h|log h|)^γ in the n=3 branch, since the L∞ bound (5.9) contributes h^{-1/2}\|∇(ẑ_h − z̄_h)\|_{L²}. The claimed rate is asserted only on the basis of 'interpolation and inverse estimates' plus the L²-estimate \|y_{ū_h} − ȳ_h\|_{L²} ≲ h². Standard finite-element theory under the available H²-regularity gives only first-order convergence for gradients (\|∇(y − y_h)\|_{L^q} ≲ h\|y\|_{H²}); a second-order gradient estimate would require W^{3,q}-type regularity or a dedicated duality argument, neither of which is available or invoked. Hence the displayed bound is unsupported and the rate (h|log h|)^γ is not established by this proof as written.

failure_location.quote: Finally, using interpolation and inverse estimates, and estimate $\|\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h}} - \bar{\mathbf{y}}_{h}\|_{\mathbf{L}^{2}(\Omega)} \lesssim h^{2}$, we obtain $\|\nabla(\mathbf{y}_{\bar{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h}} - \bar{\mathbf{y}}_{h})\|_{\mathbf{L}^{\frac{6}{5}}(\Omega)}\nlesssim h^{2}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Inside the same proof, bound the convective H^{-1} terms by the direct pairing \|b(e; ·, ẑ_h) + b(·; e, ẑ_h)\|_{H^{-1}} ≲ \|e\|_{L²}(\|ẑ_h\|_{L^∞} + \|∇ẑ_h\|_{L³}) — using the divergence-free swap (2.2) and the already-proved bound \|∇ẑ_h\|_{L⁴} ≲ 1 from (4.16) — which yields \|∇(ẑ_h − z̄_h)\|_{L²} ≲ h² and preserves every stated claim and rate.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the advertised control-variable rate (h|log h|^γ and its dependent state estimate are unsupported as written; filling the gap with the best standard estimate would halve the advertised rate.
issues.title: Unsupported O(h^2) estimate for the gradient of the state error in the control-error proof
issues.why_classification: The defective step is bypassed by re-pairing the same Hölder estimates with quantities the paper itself already bounds (\|e\|_{L²} ≲ h², \|ẑ_h\|_{W^{1,∞}} bounded); the repair is local and routine and every substantive claim and rate survives.
